detail: Serbia said it can accept the acquis on free movement of workers and expects no difficulty implementing it by accession.
Three named laws set the conditions under which a foreigner can work in Serbia.
Serbia said foreign citizens may be employed only with temporary or permanent residence and a work permit.
A non-national working in a healthcare facility must speak Serbian and any other official language in use.
Serbia said amendments on language requirements are being prepared to align the situation with the acquis.
Foreign nationals with residence and work permits may register with the employment service, with the same unemployment rights as Serbian citizens.
Employment services are free, but only foreigners with a personal work permit may register with the National Employment Service.
The Commission reports a new Law on Employment of Foreigners adopted in November 2014 to align further with the acquis.
The Commission says Serbian legislation must be amended to abolish procedures and practices impairing free movement of workers.
The Commission says mandatory language requirements may apply only in limited circumstances, where reasonable and necessary for the job.
